subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: CAUTION. Five bounded leverage candidates: (1) auto-adopt a backward-compatible typed verification evidence_ref/runId while retaining legacy command fallback; (2) user-surface one workflow-applied mutation receipt primitive reused by all readiness-affecting writes; (3) user-surface one structural session principal derived from OpenCode parentID and reused for role authority plus explicit orphan-task rescue ownership; (4) auto-adopt stage-correct non-test evidence plans—rationale/proof target at prep, review conclusion linked at acceptance, with pre-planning repair; (5) auto-adopt one actionable write-validation envelope that preserves nested Zod paths and returns remaining AC coverage after task writes. For #224/#239, reuse current bounded inventory architecture and production-shaped fixtures; do not create a second ownership path.

validation.notes: Evidence supports candidates, but agreement/contract, affected-files list, tasks, and conflict-scan prior-consideration data were unavailable in the briefing packet. Session-principal/rescue and mutation-receipt choices carry authority/replay compatibility risk and require orchestrator synthesis.

tradeoffs: Typed run references improve correctness but require backward-compatible report-schema evolution and producer updates.
Workflow-applied mutation receipts remove stale-read ambiguity but add workflow state/history and replay-compatibility obligations.
A structural session principal can unify #247 and #245, but task ownership/rescue authority must preserve peer privacy and fail closed.
Stage-correct evidence plans reduce planning dead ends but shift review-conclusion enforcement from prep to acceptance.
Richer validation responses improve repairability but increase public response-schema and fixture maintenance.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Most design choices are structurally aligned and simple: shared parentID ancestry, pure cancellation-aware projections, typed run IDs, additive legacy normalization, a bounded signal receipt fence, and reuse of existing archive/worktree authorities. Temporal documentation confirms that a receipt fence is justified under the signal-only constraint because signal() acknowledges server acceptance rather than handler application (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing; https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/main/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts). Design cannot pass as written because three authority boundaries remain unsound: OpenCode discards Zod issue details before the handler, reviewer test_run_ids lack per-reference exit-status semantics, and unrestricted review_conclusion task updates can satisfy a reviewer-owned completion condition by string presence (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L120-L176; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L352-L379; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/validator/task-classifier.ts#L253-L319).

blockers: AC4 blocker: proposed custom Zod union error callback cannot make SDK pre-handler failures carry nested paths. OpenCode converts plugin Zod validation to Schema.declare((u) => zodParams.safeParse(u).success), discarding ZodError issues, and public plugin ToolDefinition exposes no formatValidationError hook (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L120-L176; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/plugin/src/tool.ts#L42-L55).

AC6 blocker: reviewer verification gains only test_run_ids while its schema reports aggregate pass|fail|n/a, not expected exit status per referenced run; therefore the stated typed-v1 rule 'same-task run ID and matching reported exit status' is undefined for reviewer reports (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L352-L379; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L404-L489).

AC5 blocker: adding caller-writable review_conclusion as a generic pre-planning repair field can satisfy current presence-based completion validity without proof that a reviewer produced the conclusion; completion authority must instead validate a typed persisted reviewer-report reference or equivalent reviewer-owned fact (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/validator/task-classifier.ts#L253-L319).
validation.notes: No contract compromise found in session ancestry, warning-only orphan visibility, coverage semantics, receipt fencing, archive budget reuse, poison isolation, or additive replay strategy. Cache correctness remains a caution: session.updated and session.deleted are official lifecycle events, so ancestry cache invalidation must clear all dependent entries—or simplest, omit caching—rather than only the deleted session key (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts).

tradeoffs: Signal receipt fencing adds one query surface, bounded wait latency, FIFO state, and replay fixtures, but preserves the repository's signal-only workflow contract while giving application acknowledgement that Signal RPC alone does not provide (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing).

Strict pre-handler validation preserves rejection-before-persistence but, under current OpenCode host plumbing, prevents ADV handler-owned rich diagnostics because failed Zod issues are reduced to a boolean predicate (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L120-L176).

Typed evidence refs remove command-label authority and improve structural matching, but every report variant needs explicit expected-outcome semantics plus legacy provenance maintenance (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L404-L489).

alternatives_considered.option: Keep custom Zod union error callback as sole SDK pre-handler diagnostic mechanism
alternatives_considered.rationale: OpenCode checks only safeParse(...).success for plugin arguments and discards issues, so callback messages cannot reach the model-facing validation error (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L120-L176).

alternatives_considered.option: Add OpenCode plugin validation-error formatter plumbing while retaining strict report schema
alternatives_considered.rationale: Preserves strict pre-handler rejection and exposes bounded ADV-formatted nested issues at the actual host boundary; requires coordinated OpenCode/plugin API support because ToolDefinition currently lacks that field (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/plugin/src/tool.ts#L42-L55).

alternatives_considered.option: Loosen report field admission and validate only inside ADV handler
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would make actionable handler diagnostics possible but contradicts approved strict-schema/no-loose-admission direction and shifts malformed payloads past the SDK boundary (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/docs/specs/subagent-reports.md).

alternatives_considered.option: Use one common typed test-run reference object carrying run ID and expected exit code across engineer, designer, and reviewer reports
alternatives_considered.rationale: Gives every variant the same unambiguous same-task/run/exit comparison while leaving command labels descriptive (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L74-L80; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L352-L379).

alternatives_considered.option: Use aggregate reviewer results to infer exit-status matching
alternatives_considered.rationale: Inference is ambiguous for multiple runs and n/a, and the design does not define pass/fail aggregation semantics (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L367-L373).

alternatives_considered.option: Use Temporal Update for readiness-affecting writes
alternatives_considered.rationale: Updates are the canonical synchronous mutation/result mechanism, but the approved repository contract explicitly preserves signal-only change workflows; receipt query fencing is the simpler compliant alternative within that constraint (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing).

alternatives_considered.option: Use cache refresh, fixed sleep, or command-label matching as authority
alternatives_considered.rationale: These do not prove application or typed evidence identity; Signal RPC only proves server acceptance, and existing command matching is label-coupled (https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/main/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/trunk/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L404-L489).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Do not approve design gate yet. Amend only three internal mechanisms without expanding scope: establish a real OpenCode pre-handler diagnostic transport (or explicitly revise AC4 with orchestrator decision), define one typed run-reference/outcome shape for every task-scoped report variant, and make reviewer conclusion authority a validated persisted reviewer-report reference rather than caller-authored plan text. Also state cache-wide/dependency-aware invalidation or remove ancestry caching. Then rerun design validation.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Hold design gate. Correct AC4 transport feasibility, AC6 reviewer outcome semantics, and AC5 reviewer-owned conclusion linkage; preserve remaining shared-authority, receipt-fence, compatibility, and scale decisions.
follow_ups: Clarify whether 'cache cleared on session deletion' means whole-cache/dependent-entry invalidation; if not, remove caching or invalidate descendants on session.updated/session.deleted (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts).

Add design-level tests proving SDK-pre-handler malformed nested reports expose bounded paths without handler execution; current OpenCode host source predicts failure until formatter plumbing changes (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/67caf894e0843ee370e72839e8265e483233479b/packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts#L120-L176).

# Proposal: Fix workflow reliability defects

## Why

Recent production use exposed nine related ADV workflow reliability defects. Some block orchestration, execution, acceptance, or archive outright; others turn typed evidence and recovery into repeated manual retries. Existing fixes for archive scale and bounded worktree inspection need production-shaped confirmation before their GitHub issues can be considered resolved.

## What Changes

- Correct main-session authority classification while preserving fail-closed sub-agent restrictions.
- Surface tasks stranded by dead peer sessions and document a bounded recovery procedure.
- Make contract-reference coverage semantics visible at task-write boundaries.
- Return actionable nested validation failures for malformed sub-agent reports.
- Ensure readiness decisions observe accepted workflow mutations without a false one-cycle retry.
- Make non-test evidence routes satisfiable across prep and later review stages.
- Bind verification evidence structurally rather than relying on exact display-command equality.
- Validate archive conflict authority and worktree cleanup against production-shaped scale and poisoned-history cases.

## User Outcomes

- Main ADV sessions can run orchestrator-only tools consistently.
- A dead peer session cannot leave an in-progress task invisible; ADV identifies the orphan and presents the existing recovery procedure.
- Agents receive precise, actionable guidance when contract or report payloads are invalid.
- Valid evidence plans pass prep with stage-appropriate proof and acquire review proof before completion.
- Recorded verification evidence remains recognized when human-readable report labels differ cosmetically.
- Gate completion reflects successful preceding mutations on the first valid attempt.
- Large projects can archive and inspect worktrees without terminal-history volume or one poisoned workflow wedging unrelated work.
- Each affected GitHub issue receives deterministic regression evidence or an explicit already-fixed validation result.

## Affected Code

Plugin role-firewall/session hooks, Temporal task state and session diagnostics, task/contract validators, sub-agent report schemas and consumers, readiness mutation/query ordering, active conflict authority, and worktree registry inspection.

## Related Repositories

- `Sharper-Flow/Advance` only.
- External project incidents provide reproduction evidence but require no application-repository changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve fail-closed role and gate enforcement.
- Preserve peer-session privacy; do not expose peer PIDs or private working directories.
- Preserve Temporal determinism, signal ordering, replay compatibility, and Temporal-only runtime persistence.
- Prefer typed identifiers, schemas, workflow state, and explicit recovery evidence over string heuristics or timeout guesses.
- Coordinate with existing `addArchiveScaleRegression`; do not duplicate its #239 implementation ownership.
- Preserve backward compatibility through additive schema evolution and explicit legacy fallbacks.

## Impact

High reliability impact across proposal-through-release workflows. Public tool schemas and workflow state may evolve additively; generated schemas, replay-aware tests, targeted regressions, smoke verification, and full-suite validation are required.

## Context

GitHub issues in scope: #224, #239, #240, #241, #243, #244, #245, #246, and #247.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Investigation, regression reproduction, implementation, verification, and GitHub-resolution evidence for the nine named issues.
- Public schemas, docs, and generated artifacts needed by confirmed fixes.
- Coordination with `addArchiveScaleRegression` for #239 validation.

### Out of Scope

- Unrelated older GitHub issues.
- Application-project repair operations or destructive cleanup of existing archives/worktrees.
- Broad replacement of Temporal, OpenCode session architecture, or ADV gate policy.
- Automatic reset, completion, or cancellation of orphaned tasks.

### Must Not

- Do not weaken sub-agent role restrictions.
- Do not auto-complete or silently reset orphaned tasks.
- Do not count `respects` as implementation or verification coverage.
- Do not accept display command text as verification authority without typed evidence.
- Do not add archive conflict-check bypasses that permit false clean conclusions.

# Discovery Findings

## Discovery Checklist

| Step | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Skill discovery | PASS | Loaded `adv-agent-tool-contracts` and `adv-audit`; no new skill gap. |
| Prior research extension | PASS | Extended `gateAgentToolsRole`, `refineTestEvidencePolicy`, `fixAcceptanceReadiness`, `fixChangeEnumerationStarvation`, and `parallelizeStoreMaintenance`. |
| Conflict scan | PASS, degraded terminal context | 99 changes enumerated; 4 archive candidates omitted. Active authority remained conclusive and target validation passed with expected `NO_TASKS`/`NO_DELTAS`. |
| Edge cases | PASS | Two or more failure modes recorded for every confirmed gap. |
| Design questions | PASS | Technical choices bounded for design; user outcome choices resolved. |
| Draft spec deltas | PASS | Six draft law changes identified; #239/#224 remain regression-only against existing laws. |
| Related-pattern scan | PASS | Similar session, validation, evidence, readiness, and bounded-inventory patterns mapped. |
| LBP check | PASS | Typed ancestry, evidence references, stage-correct proof, actionable validation, and applied-mutation receipts are preferred. |
| Completeness verification | PASS | Primary and secondary surfaces classified; no unverified sole-entry claim remains. |

## Skills Considered

- `adv-agent-tool-contracts`: applies to report schemas, tool arguments, packets, generated schemas, and parity tests.
- `adv-audit`: applies to spec-to-code drift and requirement/test mapping.
- `adv-opportunity-scout`: researcher pass considered five candidates; three low-risk contract-tied candidates auto-adopted.
- No skill creation required.

## Extends

- `gateAgentToolsRole`: established fail-closed session-role gating. New finding: first-transform capture is not authoritative; SDK `parentID` ancestry identifies root versus descendant structurally.
- `refineTestEvidencePolicy`: established normalized evidence plans. New finding: review conclusions are enforced too early during prep and cannot be repaired through `adv_task_update`.
- `fixAcceptanceReadiness`: fixed stale acceptance criteria snapshots and revision fencing. New finding: #243 is a distinct client acknowledgment race—signal acceptance can precede async handler application.
- `fixChangeEnumerationStarvation`: separated active conflict authority from terminal history. New finding: current implementation is correct; #239 now needs incident-scale end-to-end closure evidence, owned by `addArchiveScaleRegression`.
- `parallelizeStoreMaintenance`: bounded unrelated maintenance scans. New finding: #224 uses independent per-change worktree queries and typed poison isolation, but existing mixed-failure fixtures are too small.
- Episode recall returned one irrelevant global test memory; it was ignored and did not establish any decision.

## Conflict Scan

- Active overlap: `addArchiveScaleRegression` owns #239 regression implementation and has five completed tasks. This change consumes its accepted evidence rather than duplicating code.
- Archived related work informs but does not conflict: `gateAgentToolsRole`, `refineTestEvidencePolicy`, `fixAcceptanceReadiness`, `fixChangeEnumerationStarvation`, `parallelizeStoreMaintenance`.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Seven shared authorities address scoped defects:

1. Typed, uncached OpenCode session ancestry for root/descendant identity.
2. Pure contract-coverage and stage-aware evidence projections.
3. Canonical strict tool schemas plus narrowly looser SDK transport admission where host validation hides nested errors.
4. Durable typed test-run and reviewer-report references.
5. Workflow-applied mutation receipts for readiness writes.
6. Replay-stable acceptance patch-marker consumption.
7. Contract-tied, in-scope, advisory design-validator findings.

Existing archive/worktree authorities remain; #239 evidence comes from `addArchiveScaleRegression`, while #224 gains a 250-owner mixed-poison fixture.

## Key Decisions

### Session principal and orphan visibility

Create `utils/session-principal.ts` from existing worktree ancestry traversal. Maximum depth 10; missing/mismatched records, malformed parents, cycles, depth exhaustion, or SDK failure produce typed unresolved state. No persistent cache owns correctness. Root-only tools fail closed; union-floor reads remain available.

The role firewall and worktree root lookup reuse this resolver. `adv_wip_state` joins in-progress assignment IDs with privacy-safe live session IDs and emits at most 50 warning-only orphan rows. Unavailable peer data produces `annotations_unavailable`; no task mutation, PID, or full workdir exposure.

### Contract coverage

Extract cancellation-aware `projectContractCoverage(change)`. Only `implements`/`verifies` cover success/acceptance criteria; `respects` remains constraint/avoidance traceability. Prep and task-write responses reuse the projection and return uncovered IDs.

### Actionable report validation

OpenCode host validation discards nested Zod issues before execution; OpenCode-core modification is out of scope.

ADV tool definitions gain optional `transportArgs`. Canonical `args` continue to own plugin preflight, ADV inventory/catalog, warrants, and contract checks. `transportArgs` goes only to OpenCode `tool()`; registration enforces identical top-level keys. For report submission, host admits a report object, then strict plugin preflight validates `ScopedSubagentReportSchema` before handler/signal/write and returns at most 10 bounded path/message rows.

Because OpenCode derives its own displayed schema from transport args, tests must name this tradeoff explicitly: ADV’s canonical catalog remains strict; host admission is intentionally object-shaped only for this tool. No claim that OpenCode’s host schema remains strict.

### Stage-v2 evidence authority

`resolveTaskEvidence()` remains legacy normalizer. `validateTaskEvidenceForStage(task, prep|completion, reports)` enforces:

- prep: policy, proof target, compatible TDD intent, bounded rationale;
- completion: prep validity plus `review_evidence_ref` resolving to persisted task-scoped reviewer evidence.

Task update can repair policy/proof/rationale before planning closes, but callers cannot write reviewer references. Reviewer report ingestion writes the reference. New plans carry `stage-v2`; historical plans may read legacy `review_conclusion`, which is not authority for new plans.

Modify `rq-TDD013evp` and prep-readiness law explicitly; add completion scenarios.

### Typed report evidence

New engineer/designer verification rows reference `test_run_id`. Report sidecar metadata records `evidence_binding_version: typed-v1`; historical missing markers normalize to `legacy-command-v0`.

Typed-v1 requires same-task durable run ID and matching exit status; command text is descriptive. Reviewer aggregate prose never proves runs. Historical reports retain exact-command fallback only. Worker packet, prompt, schema, consumer, and asset tests change together.

### Readiness receipts

Verification dispositions, design dispositions, contract review matrices, and executive-summary/acceptance-proof updates carry unique optional `mutationReceiptId`. Workflow records exact IDs after successful apply/readiness update in deterministic FIFO state capped at 100.

Generalize existing bounded query polling into `waitForQueryPredicate`; `waitForAppliedReceipt` sends signal, confirms exact receipt, refreshes, then returns success. Timeout/completed/query failure returns `MUTATION_APPLICATION_UNCONFIRMED`; cache changes, delays, another mutation, or blind retry never prove application.

### TMPRL1100 replay repair

Observed evidence:

`[TMPRL1100] Nondeterminism error: Non-deprecated patch marker encountered for change state-backed-acceptance-proof-v1, but there is no corresponding change command!`

Every acceptance `gateCompleted` attempt evaluates `wf.patched(STATE_BACKED_ACCEPTANCE_PROOF_PATCH)` once before readiness/artifact branch-dependent early returns and reuses the boolean. Marker ID remains unchanged and is never deprecated while matching histories exist.

Add exact replay fixture where history contains marker but current state already has artifact evidence, plus retain legacy/state-backed fixtures. Build/deploy worker, then restart Advance and PokeEdge Web workers only with explicit operator approval evidence. Run bounded read-only target queries for `fixSetLogoLoading`, `addAppIcons`, `restoreUpgradePageChrome`, archived `refinePopulationPanel`, and additional open candidates. No product task/gate/status/archive mutation occurs.

### Validator scope

For new `researcher:design-validation` reports, blocker rows require finding, source, approved contract IDs, `scope: in_scope`, and in-scope remediation. Out-of-scope alternatives belong only in `alternatives_considered`. Handler rejects malformed blocker authority; legacy reports remain readable.

Command/agent assets state `validation.status: fail` is advisory, cannot hold/complete gates, and pauses only for independently established contract compromise, security/release blocker, or real conflict.

### Scale evidence

- #239: consume owner change’s 250-terminal/50-active, zero-terminal-read, fixed-8-second evidence.
- #224: >=250 owners with healthy, poisoned, omitted outcomes; omissions never deletion candidates.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Create ADV worktree; port tested #247 bootstrap diff.
2. Add RED tests for replay marker, transport/canonical parity, nested errors, stage-v2 evidence, typed run binding, receipts, validator scope, orphan privacy, and scale.
3. Implement pure authorities/schemas, then consumers and prompt/assets.
4. Apply typed spec deltas, including `rq-TDD013evp`, prep/completion evidence law, replay compatibility, session authority, report diagnostics, receipts, and validator scope.
5. Run worker replay suite, targeted clusters, schema generation/check, `pnpm run check`, build, smoke, and full suite.
6. Deploy and approval-gated worker restart; query PokeEdge target read-only.
7. Produce issue/workflow closure evidence without bypassing product gates.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred design uses typed IDs, deterministic workflow state, pure projections, explicit versioned compatibility, bounded outputs, and one authority per decision.

Rejected: first-transform identity, persistent correctness caches, timeout orphan reset, `respects` coverage, OpenCode-core edits, loose handler ingest, caller-authored reviewer authority, reviewer prose as run proof, fuzzy command normalization, delay/cache retry as mutation proof, Temporal Updates, marker removal/deprecation, recovery bypass, validator gate holds, duplicate inventories, or raised budgets.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- ancestry depth <=10; no persistent correctness cache;
- orphan rows <=50 and privacy-safe;
- canonical/transport top-level keys exactly equal;
- nested error rows <=10 and bounded bytes;
- new non-test plans use stage-v2 reviewer-owned evidence;
- typed runs match same task and exit status;
- receipt FIFO <=100 and exact-ID confirmation;
- acceptance marker evaluated before branch-dependent returns;
- PokeEdge nonterminal workflows query without fallback after deployment;
- validator blockers cite approved contract IDs and in-scope remediation;
- worktree fixture >=250; archive budget remains 8 seconds with zero terminal authority reads;
- worker restart requires explicit operator approval evidence;
- generated schemas and replay fixtures remain deterministic.

## Risks / Mitigations

- Shared-authority blast radius: caller-parity and legacy fixtures first.
- Host transport schema is broader: immediate strict plugin preflight; same-key invariant; no mutation before parse; ADV canonical catalog remains strict.
- Replay regression: preserve marker ID/location within acceptance handler; exact poisoned-history fixture.
- State growth: receipt FIFO capped at 100.
- Legacy evidence: explicit stage/evidence-binding versions, never timestamp inference.
- False orphan warning: warning-only and typed unavailable source status.
- Cross-project safety: explicit target confirmation; approval-gated worker restart; query-only validation.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Adopted early patch consumption, shared receipt predicate, uncached session principal. Designed around transport/canonical schema parity and one stage-aware evidence validator. No user-value tradeoff.

## Independent Validator Result

**CAUTION; no blocker.** Validator confirmed replay repair and structural direction. Required cautions incorporated:

- explicit `rq-TDD013evp` and prep-readiness deltas;
- tests distinguish strict ADV canonical catalog from intentionally broad OpenCode host admission;
- worker restart is approval-gated; target checks remain read-only.

Previous validator overreach was reconciled: useful SDK/reviewer findings retained, OpenCode-core modification and gate hold rejected as out of scope/unauthorized.

## Contract-Compromise Assessment

None. All 40 contract items remain satisfiable without gate bypass, PokeEdge product edits, OpenCode-core changes, or new dependencies.
